subject: Request: Temporary QPS uplift + escrowed overrun arrangement
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@brightcart.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Temporary QPS uplift + escrowed overrun arrangement

Hi Tessa —

We’re ramping to a big promotional launch next month and expect a short, high-volume window (estimated 48–72 hours) where traffic to our chat and product-recommendation routes will spike ~3x baseline. We’d like Redwood to temporarily raise our QPS/rate limit and allow a per-route override for that window.

To avoid surprises on both sides, procurement would prefer to pre-fund an escrow account that we draw from for any overrun tokens during the window. Our initial thinking: pre-fund $25,000 into escrow, Redwood invoices any excess beyond that from the next billing cycle (true-up), and if the escrow is not fully consumed we apply remaining credit to the subsequent invoice.

Can you confirm whether:
- Redwood can open a 72-hour boost window with per-route overrides (we need a dedicated override for /api/v1/recommend and /api/v1/chat).
- You support an escrow/prepay flow (we’ll provide a PO).
- The true-up timeline is month-end reconciliation or do you do an earlier cut for one-off uplift windows?

I’ve attached a short traffic forecast and peak QPS estimate. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps. Also, procurement asked whether there’s any concession on unit pricing for pre-funded overrun coverage — they mentioned a desire for a one-time discount for the escrowed dollars.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Engineering, BrightCart
attachments: BrightCart_launch_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, forecast)
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Sam Patel <sam@brightcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary QPS uplift + escrowed overrun arrangement

Sam —

Thanks for the details and the forecast. We can support what you describe; below are two practical options and the trade-offs so procurement can pick which path they prefer:

Option A — Short boost window (recommended for launches)
- 72-hour window where we apply a temporary per-route QPS override.
- Pre-fundable escrow: you pre-pay an agreed dollar amount (credited to your account). Any consumption during the window reduces the escrow in real time.
- True-up: we run a reconciliation at the end of the month and bill any additional overrun beyond escrow on the next invoice. Credits for unused escrow apply to the following invoice.

Option B — Immediate card pre-auth for fast start
- We can provision the override faster if you pre-authorize a corporate card for a temporary hold. This avoids PO timing but procurement usually prefers Option A.

Pricing notes and discount ask
- Base unit pricing during the boost uses your existing model SKU rates. For the escrowed dollars, we can offer a one-time uplift discount on consumed overrun dollars (we typically do 5–10% for pre-funded commitments).
- If you’re asking for a steeper concession (15%+), we’ll need the deal team to review (linking Ben and Kim).

Next steps
1) Confirm preferred option (A or B) and exact window start/end in UTC.
2) Provide PO number and billing contact for Option A, or provide card pre-auth for Option B.
3) We’ll prepare a short temporary-amendment (SOW) that outlines the boost window, escrow mechanics, reconciliation timing, and rollback/fallback behavior if we detect sustained above-threshold traffic.

Ben — can you confirm the per-route override ceilings and any technical limits we should call out in the SOW? Kim — please flag the billing/discount constraints.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_temp_amendment_v1.pdf (draft will follow)
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Sam Patel <sam@brightcart.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary QPS uplift + escrowed overrun arrangement

Sam —

Quick technical clarifications from the runtime side:
- Per-route override: we can create route-specific QPS ceilings for /api/v1/recommend and /api/v1/chat. For a 3x spike we typically set a soft ceiling at the requested peak and a hard ceiling ~20% above to handle microbursts.
- Model fallback: we can configure an automatic, penalty-free fallback to a smaller quantized model if latency or capacity constraints are triggered. That keeps user surface-area available while lowering unit cost if invoked.
- Cost model during uplift: overrides are charged at your existing SKU rates; the escrow is drawn down against the actual tokens consumed. We can apply a multiplier on the last-mile per-token price if you require guaranteed headroom beyond X qps — let us know if you want the guarantee.
- Reconciliation: standard is month-end true-up. For this window we can do an interim reconciliation 7 business days after the uplift to settle the escrow faster if that helps procurement.

Operational ask: we’ll need the exact routes and an estimated peak QPS per route (numbers in your attached forecast look helpful; please confirm). Also need a billing contact and PO to generate the escrow invoice.

If you want to push for a deeper discount on the escrowed dollars, that’s a commercial conversation; I can model what a 10% and 15% concession would do to uplift economics and share by EOD.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Patel <sam@brightcart.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary QPS uplift + escrowed overrun arrangement

Thanks Tessa and Ben —

We’ll go with Option A (escrow pre-fund). Procurement is drafting a PO for $25,000 for the initial window. PO draft attached.

A couple of points from procurement and product:
1) Can Redwood guarantee that the boost window will not be automatically terminated mid-window due to unrelated capacity events? We need an explicit failback clause: if Redwood must throttle the account for platform health reasons, we want a 10-minute notice and documented rollback plan.
2) Procurement is asking whether the escrowed dollars can be refunded if less than 60% is consumed. They’d prefer either a partial refund or a credit at a 1.0x rate rather than forcing a credit subject to discount.
3) On discounts: BrightCart is a strategic customer; we’re asking whether Redwood can offer a 15% concession on the escrowed dollars (applied to any consumption from escrow).

Expected peaks: /api/v1/recommend : 120 qps peak, /api/v1/chat : 220 qps peak. Peak window start: 2026-10-20T18:00:00Z — estimated 72 hours.

We want the temporary-amendment and the final invoice/true-up cadence documented so procurement can approve the PO quickly.

Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Engineering, BrightCart
attachments: PO_draft_BrightCart.pdf (procurement draft)
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Sam Patel <sam@brightcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary QPS uplift + escrowed overrun arrangement

Sam —

Appreciate the clear numbers and the PO draft. We can proceed with Option A under the following terms (summary for procurement/legal):

1) Window and overrides
- Temporary boost window: 2026-10-20T18:00:00Z to 2026-10-23T18:00:00Z (72 hours).
- Per-route ceilings set to your requested peaks with a 20% hard ceiling buffer.
- Failure handling: Redwood will not pre-emptively terminate a customer boost window for normal capacity reasons. If platform-wide emergency action is required we will provide a 10-minute warning via email and SMS to the designated on-call contact, and we will document rollback steps. (This will be included in the temporary amendment.)

2) Escrow and reconciliation
- We will accept the PO for $25,000 as an escrowed prepayment. Any consumption during the boost will draw down the escrow in real time.
- Reconciliation: standard month-end true-up applies. Given the launch timing we’ll also run an interim reconciliation 7 business days after 2026-10-23 to settle escrow consumption early.
- Unused funds: any remaining escrow balance will be applied as a credit to your next invoice at 1.0x (no discount applied to residuals). We cannot process cash refunds for standard SOC reasons; credit is the default.

3) Discount request
- We can offer a one-time 7.5% concession on consumed escrow dollars (i.e., any usage drawn from the escrow during the boost window will receive a 7.5% discount). We’re not able to approve 15% as a unilateral concession without exec review. If BrightCart needs 15% we can route that for approval but timing is not guaranteed.

4) Contracting and execution
- I’ve uploaded a short temporary-amendment (DocuSign link below) which captures the window, escalation contact, escrow mechanics, and reconciliation timing. Please return a signed copy and the PO number so billing can issue the escrow invoice.

DocuSign (temporary amendment): https://www.docusign.com/temporary-amendment/ABC-123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

If that is acceptable we’ll generate the escrow invoice on receipt of the PO. Ben will also coordinate on the per-route ceilings and model-fallback configuration.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth launch for BrightCart.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
